Panellets (Catalan Almond Cookies)

Served at: Immaculada

Makes about 30-35 cookiesPrep 45 minCook 8-12 min

Panellets are traditional Catalan sweets, small marzipan-based cookies, most famously enjoyed during La Castanyada (All Saints' Day) on November 1st. Their rich almond flavor and festive appearance make them a delightful treat throughout the autumn and early winter, perfectly suited for sharing with loved ones during the Immaculada holiday on December 8th.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (250 g) almond flour
  • 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) cooked and mashed potato (or sweet potato), cooled
  • Zest of 1 large lemon
  • 1 large egg, lightly beaten (for the dough)
  • 1 large egg yolk, lightly beaten (for glazing)
  • 3/4 cup (100 g) pine nuts
  • 1/2 cup (50 g) shredded coconut
  • 1 tablespoon unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 1 teaspoon instant coffee powder (optional, for coffee flavor)
  • Candied fruit, chopped (for decoration, optional)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the almond flour, granulated sugar, and lemon zest. Mix well.
  2. Add the cooled mashed potato and the lightly beaten egg to the dry ingredients. Mix with your hands until a cohesive, firm dough forms. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more almond flour; if too dry, add a tiny bit more mashed potato or egg white.
  3. Divide the dough into 3-4 equal portions. Leave one portion plain for pine nut panellets.
  4. For coconut panellets: Knead shredded coconut into one portion of dough until well combined.
  5. For chocolate panellets: Knead cocoa powder into another portion of dough until evenly colored.
  6. For coffee panellets (optional): Dissolve instant coffee powder in a tiny amount of hot water (about 1/2 tsp) and knead into a portion of dough.
  7. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  8. From the plain dough, roll small balls, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) in diameter. Roll these balls in pine nuts, pressing gently so the nuts adhere all over the surface. Place them on the prepared baking sheet.
  9. From the coconut dough, roll small balls or cone shapes. Place them on the baking sheet.
  10. From the chocolate dough, roll small balls or logs. Place them on the baking sheet.
  11. From the coffee dough, roll small balls or other shapes. Place them on the baking sheet.
  12. Brush the tops of all the panellets, especially the pine nut ones, with the lightly beaten egg yolk. For coconut panellets, you can leave them unglazed or brush lightly.
  13. Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until the panellets are lightly golden brown. Be careful not to overbake, as they can dry out quickly. The pine nuts should be toasted.
  14. Remove from the oven and let cool completely on a wire rack before serving. Decorate chocolate or plain panellets with small pieces of candied fruit if desired.

Tips

  • For best texture, use a starchy potato like Russet, boiled until very soft and mashed smoothly without lumps.
  • Panellets can be made a day in advance and stored in an airtight container at room temperature.
  • Experiment with other flavors like finely ground pistachios, orange zest, or a touch of cinnamon in the dough.
